title: Matthew Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 11.

questions.question: In Matthew 11, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus began to say concerning John
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in Matthew 11:1.

questions.question: Who sent two of his disciples to Jesus?
questions.explanation: John sent two of his disciples to Jesus, as stated in Matthew 11:2.

questions.question: What did John ask Jesus through his disciples?
options: Are you the one who should come?
questions.correctAnswer: Are you the one who should come?
questions.explanation: John asked if Jesus was the one who should come or if they should look for another, as per Matthew 11:3.

questions.question: What did Jesus tell John's disciples to show him?
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed them to show John the things they hear and see, referring to the works of Christ, as indicated in Matthew 11:4.

questions.question: What miracles are mentioned in Matthew 11:5?
options: The blind see and the lame walk
The deaf hear and the dead are raised
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:5 lists multiple miracles: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, and the dead are raised.

questions.question: Who is blessed according to Matthew 11:6?
options: Whosoever shall not be offended in Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Whosoever shall not be offended in Jesus
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:6 states that blessed is he who is not offended in Jesus.

questions.question: What did Jesus say the people went out to see in the wilderness?
options: A reed shaken with the wind
questions.correctAnswer: A reed shaken with the wind
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:7, Jesus asks if they went out to see a reed shaken by the wind.

questions.question: What kind of clothing did Jesus mention in Matthew 11:8?
questions.explanation: Jesus refers to those who wear soft clothing, indicating they are found in kings' houses, as stated in Matthew 11:8.

questions.question: How did Jesus describe John in relation to being a prophet?
questions.explanation: Jesus declared that John is more than a prophet, as stated in Matthew 11:9.

questions.question: What is written about the messenger in Matthew 11:10?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:10 states that the messenger will prepare the way before Jesus.

questions.question: Jesus had made an end of commanding his twelve disciples before he departed to do what?
options: Teach and preach in their cities
questions.correctAnswer: Teach and preach in their cities
questions.explanation: According to Matthew 11:1, after commanding his disciples, Jesus departed to teach and preach in their cities.

questions.question: True or False: John was in prison when he sent his disciples to Jesus.
questions.explanation: This is true as John was in prison when he heard of the works of Christ, as stated in Matthew 11:2.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus mentioned that the dead are raised in Matthew 11:5.
questions.explanation: This is true because Matthew 11:5 mentions that the dead are raised up.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said that only prophets wear soft clothing.
questions.explanation: This is false as Jesus stated that those who wear soft clothing are in kings' houses, not just prophets, as indicated in Matthew 11:8.

questions.question: True or False: The messenger mentioned in Matthew 11:10 was to be sent after Jesus' ministry.
questions.explanation: This is false because the messenger is to prepare the way before Jesus, indicating he comes before Jesus' ministry, as stated in Matthew 11:10.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who is considered greater than John the Baptist according to Jesus?
options: The least in the kingdom of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: The least in the kingdom of heaven
questions.explanation: This is stated in Matthew 11:11, where Jesus says that among those born of women, none is greater than John the Baptist, yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

questions.question: What is promised in Matthew 11:15 for those who have ears to hear?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:15 states, 'He that hath ears to hear, let him hear,' implying that those who listen will gain understanding.

questions.question: What does Matthew 11:12 indicate about the kingdom of heaven?
options: It is a place of joy
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:12 says, 'the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force,' indicating the challenges faced by the kingdom.

questions.question: In Matthew 11:13, who does Jesus say prophesied until John?
options: All the prophets and the law
questions.correctAnswer: All the prophets and the law
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:13 states that 'For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John,' emphasizing John's role in the prophetic line.

questions.question: What comparison does Jesus make about the generation in Matthew 11:16?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:16, Jesus compares the generation to children sitting in the markets, highlighting their lack of responsiveness.

questions.question: What did the people say about John in Matthew 11:18?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:18 states that John came neither eating nor drinking, and they accused him of having a devil.

questions.question: What accusation was made against the Son of Man in Matthew 11:19?
options: He is a glutton and a winebibber
questions.correctAnswer: He is a glutton and a winebibber
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:19 records that the Son of Man was accused of being gluttonous and a friend of sinners, contrasting with John's lifestyle.

questions.question: What does Matthew 11:20 indicate about cities where Jesus performed mighty works?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:20, Jesus began to upbraid the cities where He performed mighty works because they did not repent.

questions.question: What does Jesus imply about wisdom in Matthew 11:19?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:19 concludes with 'But wisdom is justified of her children,' indicating that true wisdom is shown through its effects.

questions.question: According to Matthew 11:4, what did Jesus tell John's disciples to show him?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:4, Jesus tells John's disciples to show him the works they hear and see, which includes miracles.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about those who are not offended in Him in Matthew 11:6?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:6 states, 'And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me,' indicating the blessing for those who accept Him.

questions.question: What did Jesus imply about the expectations of the people in Matthew 11:17?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:17, Jesus points out that the children were calling for dancing and mourning, reflecting the people's expectation of entertainment.

questions.question: True or False: John the Baptist was considered the greatest prophet according to Matthew 11:11.
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:11 declares that among those born of women, none is greater than John the Baptist.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus began to praise the cities where most of His mighty works were done in Matthew 11:20.
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:20, Jesus actually began to upbraid those cities for not repenting despite the mighty works done there.

questions.question: True or False: The prophets ceased to prophesy after John the Baptist according to Matthew 11:13.
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:13 states that all the prophets and the law prophesied until John, indicating that prophecy was ongoing.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 11.

questions.question: According to Matthew 11:21, what would have happened if the mighty works done in Chorazin and Bethsaida had been done in Tyre and Sidon?
options: They would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes
They would have persecuted the prophets
They would have rejoiced and celebrated
questions.correctAnswer: They would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:21 states that if the mighty works done in Chorazin and Bethsaida had been done in Tyre and Sidon, those cities would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

questions.question: What does Jesus say about Tyre and Sidon in comparison to Chorazin and Bethsaida in Matthew 11:22?
options: It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you
They shall be punished more severely
They will receive a greater blessing
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:22 says Jesus declares it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment than for Chorazin and Bethsaida.

questions.question: What fate does Jesus predict for Capernaum in Matthew 11:23?
options: Shalt be brought down to hell
Shalt be exalted above all cities
questions.correctAnswer: Shalt be brought down to hell
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:23 states that Capernaum, which is exalted unto heaven, shall be brought down to hell.

questions.question: According to Matthew 11:24, how will the judgment for the land of Sodom compare to that of Capernaum?
options: It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee
It will be less severe for Capernaum
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:24 explains that judgment will be more tolerable for Sodom than for Capernaum.

questions.question: In Matthew 11:25, Jesus thanks the Father for revealing truths to which group?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:25 states Jesus thanks the Father because He has revealed these things unto babes, while hiding them from the wise and prudent.

questions.question: What invitation does Jesus extend in Matthew 11:28?
options: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest
Go ye therefore, and teach all nations
Repent for the kingdom of heaven is at hand
questions.correctAnswer: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:28 contains Jesus' invitation for all who labor and are heavy laden to come to Him for rest.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'mēkros' (μικρός) in Matthew 11:11 mean?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:11, the Greek word 'mēkros' (μικρός) means 'least' or 'small', referring to the least in the kingdom of heaven being greater than John the Baptist.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Matthew 11:21-24 when Jesus contrasts cities like Chorazin and Bethsaida with Tyre, Sidon, and Sodom?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:21-24 uses chiasm by contrasting pairs of cities with reversed ideas to emphasize judgment severity, a common Jewish literary technique.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed in Jesus' declaration in Matthew 11:10 about sending a messenger to prepare the way?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:10 quotes Malachi 3:1, which speaks of sending a messenger before the Lord to prepare His way.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with Matthew 11:28's invitation to find rest in Jesus?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 4:9-11 speaks of a sabbath rest for the people of God, connecting with Jesus' offer of rest in Matthew 11:28.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Jesus' invitation to 'Come unto me' in Matthew 11:28?
options: Jesus declares all things are delivered unto him by the Father
John the Baptist sends disciples to Jesus
Jesus upbraids the cities for not repenting
Jesus thanks the Father for revealing truths to babes
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus declares all things are delivered unto him by the Father
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:27 immediately precedes 11:28, where Jesus says all things are delivered to him by the Father.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Greek word 'yoke' (ζυγός) as used in Matthew 11:29?
options: A symbol of submission and learning
questions.correctAnswer: A symbol of submission and learning
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:29, 'yoke' (ζυγός) metaphorically symbolizes submitting to Jesus' teaching and learning from Him.

questions.question: Matthew 11:12 speaks of the kingdom of heaven suffering violence and the violent taking it by force. What does this indicate about the nature of the kingdom?
options: The kingdom is actively contested and forcefully advanced
The kingdom is passive and peaceful
The kingdom is hidden and unknown
The kingdom is delayed until the end times
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom is actively contested and forcefully advanced
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:12 indicates the kingdom of heaven experiences violent opposition and is forcefully taken, showing its contested nature.

questions.question: What is the significance of Jesus being described as 'meek and lowly in heart' in Matthew 11:29?
options: It highlights His humility and gentleness
It refers to His physical stature
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights His humility and gentleness
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:29 portrays Jesus as 'meek and lowly in heart' to emphasize His humility and gentle nature, inviting disciples to emulate Him.

questions.question: True or False: According to Matthew 11:25, Jesus thanks the Father for revealing truths to the wise and prudent.
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:25 states Jesus thanks the Father for hiding these things from the wise and prudent and revealing them to babes, not the wise and prudent.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 11:5 teach about the nature of salvation?
options: Salvation includes both spiritual and physical restoration
Salvation is only about forgiveness of sins
Salvation is purely a future hope with no present effect
Salvation depends solely on human effort
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation includes both spiritual and physical restoration
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:5 shows Jesus describing the works of the kingdom, including healing the blind, lame, lepers, deaf, raising the dead, and preaching the gospel to the poor, indicating salvation encompasses physical and spiritual renewal.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic fulfillment does Matthew 11:14 teach?
options: John the Baptist is the Elijah who was to come
John the Baptist is a new prophet unrelated to Elijah
Elijah will return only after the final judgment
John the Baptist denies the necessity of law for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: John the Baptist is the Elijah who was to come
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:14 explicitly states that John the Baptist is the Elias (Elijah) who was to come, fulfilling Malachi's prophecy about Elijah's return before the Messiah.

questions.question: What doctrine about the kingdom of heaven does Matthew 11:11 teach?
options: The least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than John the Baptist
John the Baptist is the greatest of all in the kingdom of heaven
The kingdom of heaven is only for the righteous Jews
Only prophets can enter the kingdom of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: The least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than John the Baptist
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:11 states that although John is the greatest born of women, the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he, indicating the surpassing nature of the new covenant kingdom.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 11:27 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:27 highlights that no one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son, demonstrating God's attribute of omniscience in the unique knowledge within the Trinity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly revealed in Matthew 11:28?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 11:28 Jesus invites all who labor and are heavy laden to come to Him for rest, revealing God's attribute of grace and compassionate invitation to sinners.

questions.question: How does Matthew 11:20-24 connect to the broader biblical theme of judgment?
options: It illustrates corporate judgment for unrepentant cities
It emphasizes individual salvation apart from community
It denies future judgment in favor of universal grace
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates corporate judgment for unrepentant cities
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:20-24 pronounces woes on cities that did not repent despite mighty works, highlighting the biblical theme of corporate judgment for persistent unbelief.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Matthew 11:2-3 prepare for?
options: The Messianic identity and mission of Jesus
The giving of the Mosaic Law
questions.correctAnswer: The Messianic identity and mission of Jesus
questions.explanation: John the Baptist’s inquiry in Matthew 11:2-3 about whether Jesus is the expected one highlights the unfolding recognition of Jesus’ Messianic role fulfilling Old Testament promises.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 11:25 and 11:27 teach about divine revelation?
options: Revelation is granted by God's sovereign choice to the humble
Revelation is available to all equally regardless of heart
Revelation depends on human wisdom and learning
Revelation can be earned by good works
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation is granted by God's sovereign choice to the humble
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:25 thanks God for hiding truths from the wise and revealing them to babes, while 11:27 emphasizes that no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son reveals Him, showing revelation depends on God's sovereign gracious choice.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 11:28-30 teach about sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves learning from Christ's meekness and receiving rest
Sanctification is solely self-effort and burden-bearing
Sanctification means rejection of all yokes and laws
Sanctification is about isolation from the world
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves learning from Christ's meekness and receiving rest
questions.explanation: Verses 28-30 describe coming to Jesus for rest and taking His yoke to learn from His meekness, indicating sanctification is a gracious process of discipleship and spiritual rest.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 11:7 and 11:9 teach about John the Baptist's prophetic role?
options: John is more than a prophet and the forerunner of the Messiah
John is only a minor prophet with no special role
John is a political revolutionary rather than a prophet
John denies the need for repentance
questions.correctAnswer: John is more than a prophet and the forerunner of the Messiah
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:7 and 11:9 show Jesus affirming John’s prophetic identity and his unique role preparing the way for Christ, thus more than a typical prophet.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Matthew 11:18-19 shows Jesus condoned sinful behavior by eating and drinking with sinners. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches that Jesus' association with sinners is wise and justified, not sinful
It condones gluttony and drunkenness as acceptable Christian behavior
It implies Jesus was careless about His reputation
It denies any need for holiness in Jesus' conduct
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that Jesus' association with sinners is wise and justified, not sinful
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:18-19 rebuts accusations against both John’s asceticism and Jesus’ sociability, affirming Jesus’ wisdom in associating with sinners to call them to repentance.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 11:6 teach about faith in Christ?
options: Blessing comes to those who are not offended by Christ
Offense at Christ is expected and unavoidable for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Blessing comes to those who are not offended by Christ
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:6 pronounces a blessing on those who do not stumble or take offense at Jesus, emphasizing the necessity of faith and acceptance for blessing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 11:26 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:26 states 'for so it seemed good in thy sight,' indicating God's sovereign will in revealing truth to some and hiding it from others.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Matthew 11:10 make with the Old Testament?
options: It quotes Malachi's prophecy about the messenger preparing the way
It alludes to the Exodus from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: It quotes Malachi's prophecy about the messenger preparing the way
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:10 cites the prophecy about sending a messenger before the Lord to prepare His way, directly linking John the Baptist with Malachi 3:1.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by Matthew 11:12 about the kingdom of heaven?
options: The kingdom of heaven is subject to violent opposition and forceful advance
The kingdom of heaven comes only through peaceful acceptance
The kingdom of heaven excludes the poor and oppressed
The kingdom of heaven is irrelevant to earthly realities
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom of heaven is subject to violent opposition and forceful advance
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:12 describes the kingdom suffering violence and the violent taking it by force, indicating spiritual conflict in the advance of God's reign.
